title: Decided to torture myself and try to let AI make/animate complex creatures
author: Redditry199
selftext:
![video](wkjq14xq1r2i1)

Working on a game for the fun of it but while humanoids are kinda possible to work with when it comes to actual creatures its a pain in the ass. From making to rigging to animating it is difficult to have something that is passable-ish. Anyone got any solutions?

comments.author: ByteSide_Studio
comments.body: Honestly thought it would look worse than it does, nice!

comments.author: MesquiteBarbecueChip
comments.body: the eagle needs some interpolated Z lift after each wing flap, and gliding downward while not flapping wings. dragon looks like he should be flapping his wings faster or have larger wingspan to be more physically accurate, otherwise they look better than i thought as well

replies.author: Redditry199
replies.body: Sorry I'm not sure I follow, the Z lift makes sense but his 'hunt' pose is that of a hawk catching prey his wings aren't flapping. In the start he should gain Z lift faster now that I look closer, but some of the stuff is because its isometric view and I'm kinda limited on space i can use for height. Thanks for the input.

comments.author: Adventurous_Eye_6199
comments.body: I don't think human die like that

comments.author: caxco93
comments.body: wings compress when moving back up otherwies they would create negative lift

comments.author: SoberSeahorse
comments.body: Why do they all have “auras” of a darker color. I didn’t even notice the animations cause that is all I was looking at.

comments.author: Area_Intrepid
comments.body: yeah the solution is to use references, build intentional control rigs, half the things on birds / dragons are procedural, like wings that could work through proper ik/fk for main bones with spring chain setup for the flaps, when u have controllers you only need to tell the llm to make give them procedural control like how extreme the tangents are, and how can easily adjust based on an ai video reference but taking you models and tracing it over the ai video reference u can match limbs and the like easily with about 5-10 control points on the dragon or the eagle

comments.author: jontomato
comments.body: I'm in the midst of making an [AI first game engine](https://github.com/jnemargut/sayengine). It's super early but it might be good to work alongside what you're trying to do. Being able to kinda rig what you want to do in plain language and tweak with the editor is the kinda workflow I'm figuring out.
